text: Rao Fang. In Thai, it means: we listen. It lets a farm-tour host know what every foreign guest thought of the tour. In Thai, offline, on the phone she already has.

Foreign guests leave the farm, and what they thought leaves with them. They write in English, Chinese or Korean. The host reads Thai, and the signal on the farm is weak. So she never learns what guests valued, what went wrong, or what they wanted to buy.
Meet Noor. She grows coffee in the hills of Chiang Rai, and hosts six or seven foreign visitors a month. She speaks Thai and Kham Mueang, the Northern Thai dialect. And she has one Android phone.

Rao Fang is one loop, all on that phone. The guest answers in their own language. An AI on the phone sorts the answers into tour topics. And the host reviews them in Thai. The AI suggests. The host decides.

This is the live app. A Korean guest picks their language, and agrees to a short consent. They rate each step of the tour. Then they type what could be better, and that they'd like to buy two bags of beans. They hand the phone back. Nothing leaves it.

On the weekend, the host opens her insights. How happy guests were. The top strength, and the top problem. And one card for each part of the tour. She can listen to any card in Thai, and every number opens the real guest comments behind it. Comments the AI can't sort, wait for a person.

That fail-safe matters. On our held-out test set, the app sorted sixty-nine percent of comments on its own, and ninety-one percent of those were right. The rest go to a 'not sure' list, which the host tags in two taps. That test set is synthetic. Accuracy with real guests is the next thing we measure.

It works in airplane mode. There's a one-time, one-hundred-and-ninety-seven megabyte download on Wi-Fi, and after that, no signal is needed. Speech becomes text on the phone itself, and no guest data is sent anywhere.

And it speaks the host's language. Insights are fixed Thai sentences, filled with real counts and real quotes, so there's no AI-written text to go wrong. The host can also teach it Kham Mueang words, starting with thirty-eight starter words she confirms or corrects.

For an agritourism operator, that means every host hears every guest, every week. Purchase interest is counted. Problems with directions, group size or price show up early. And there's nothing to run. No servers, no data plans, no cost per guest.
Where it stands: the app is built, it's live, and it works offline. What it hasn't had yet, is a real phone in a real field, with real guests.
So our ask is simple. Approve Rao Fang for a real season: real hosts, real guests, measured results. Try it now, at rao-fang dot vercel dot app.
